objective: Restate the 2-CNF/3-CNF boundary in relational semantics with the K1-K3 knot test: the two-loop knot is unique, no 2-CNF with witnesses defines a knot, and three-literal clauses with witnesses define every knot. Diagnose Proof 0009's executor rule (a loop's guard checked only while the loop runs supplies the loop's presence as a literal) and the old Lean kernel's erasure condition (it accepts the 2-CNF relation (A<->B) and (A->c)), and check the two-loop theorems in a Lean 4 kernel.
status: Proved by KNOT-FOUNDATION-20261019-001A-P001: K1-K3 knot is unique for two loops, no 2-CNF with witnesses defines a knot, three-literal chains define every knot; Lean 4.32.2 kernel and an independent checker.
title: Relational successor to Proof 0009: the K1-K3 width boundary with a Lean kernel
